question: Can learned intervention decisions trained by observed reward-to-go outperform conventional recurrent decisions and corrupted reward-credit when factual intervention consequences have delayed effects and reversals?
null: Reward-trained causal-feature actor fails to outperform equally trained conventional recurrent policy, incorrect credit-assignment negative and passive/random P13 controls by >=0.05 mean factual reward/action on all independent initialization seeds per known delayed environment; retained familiar competence uncertain.

architectures: CausalFeaturePolicy (20->20->1, 441 params, raw 8 factual pairs + hand-derived 0..3 temporal action/outcome correlations)
ConventionalGRUPolicy (GRU 2->10 + 10->1, 431 params, same raw 8 factual pairs)
CausalFeaturePolicy with reward-to-go shifted across time and world/episode during policy-gradient update
design.train_world_source: fresh local authored development action-consequence generator with episode lag sampled from 0..3, varying hidden action-gain sign, unknown regime change, same exogenous cohort seeds for every training class
design.optimizer: AdamW learning rate 0.003, REINFORCE reward-to-go gamma=0.97, per-time batch normalization of advantage, entropy regularization 0.01, gradient clip 3.0
design.reward_credit_negative: roll reward-to-go 16 time steps and one world across batch, preserves histogram but destroys correct factual action attribution
design.source_evaluation: UNCHANGED prior known P10 instant/lagged DEV and P12 delay2, delay3, changing_delay and no action sham DEV, four original DEV seeds each; these are NOT independently born heldout science
design.probe_schedule: all control arms forced actions at 0,4,...60; trained candidate, conventional GRU, and reward credit-negative use exact same signed action choices for these 16 slots, others may use their frozen 16-slot policy
eval_controls: equally trained and information-parity conventional GRU
same size actor reward-misalignment gradient negative
original P13 hardcoded active and passive ridge probes
design.required_support: all three model initialization seeds per each distinct authored structure; do NOT count repeated procedural world seeds as independent science
design.old_capability_retention: familiar instant and one-lag worlds must not lose more than .02 reward/action relative to conventional GRU for any of three model seeds, diagnostic; no cold process retention claimed
design.sham_invariant: exact realized reward sequence for all arms irrespective of chosen action
design.trained_actor_gradient_test: optimizer updates must actually change source weights
design.same_budget_control: same actor-reward update steps and shared world cohort, near-matched parameter count; different actor FLOPs and on-policy trajectories NOT independently matched
